correctness.rationale: Take X~Bin(21,1/2), Y=floor(3X/5), and F(t)=2^21 E[t^Y] of degree 12 with the displayed exact binomial coefficients. F has four real simple roots and four conjugate pairs: rational centers with radius 10^-5 satisfy 8 disjoint exact Taylor/Rouché inequalities, plus conjugate disks. Interval polynomial arithmetic certifies a strictly positive degree-2 factor and two strictly positive degree-5 factors, hence normalized law is P5. For any nonnegative real factorization, irreducible factors are four real linears plus four real conjugate quadratics. Conservative interval tests retain 41 possibly nonnegative groups of degree at most 4. Exhaustive subset partition DP proves that even this optimistic family cannot cover all eight irreducible factors; hence not P4 or any smaller j. Independently recomputed coefficient list, rational disk inequalities, positive 2+5+5 grouping, all 41 optimistic candidate groups, and absence of a <=4 cover. This is an exact finite rational certification of the precise 21-trial law, not a numerical-root heuristic.
